summary: The document outlines an AI‑driven HR analytics platform called HR‑Pulse, describing 20+ high‑level features such as meeting sentiment analysis, manager effectiveness scoring, promotion readiness detection, bias detection, digital twins, workforce simulation and an executive dashboard. It focuses on business value statements and presentation guidance but provides no technical architecture, data handling, security, compliance, performance, or testing details.

risk_factors.title: Employee Personal Data Exposure
risk_factors.description: The platform processes highly sensitive employee data (sentiments, health indicators, performance reviews, complaints) without any mention of data minimisation, consent, encryption, or retention policies.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define GDPR/HIPAA compliant data handling procedures, implement encryption at rest and in transit, obtain explicit employee consent, and enforce strict access controls.

risk_factors.title: AI Bias and Discrimination
risk_factors.description: Features such as Workplace Fairness Detector, Promotion Readiness AI, and Bias Detection lack any bias‑mitigation strategy, model explainability, or audit logs.
risk_factors.mitigation: Integrate bias detection pipelines, maintain model audit trails, provide explainable AI outputs, and conduct regular fairness assessments against protected attributes.

risk_factors.title: Insufficient Access Control
risk_factors.description: No authentication, role‑based access control, or audit logging is described for sensitive modules like Complaint Investigation Agent or HR Action Impact Tracker.
risk_factors.mitigation: Implement RBAC, MFA for HR administrators, and immutable audit logs for all AI‑driven decisions.

risk_factors.title: Model Drift and Reliability
risk_factors.description: Continuous AI predictions (burnout, attrition, conflict) are proposed without monitoring, retraining, or validation processes.
risk_factors.mitigation: Establish model monitoring dashboards, schedule periodic retraining with fresh data, and define performance thresholds with rollback mechanisms.

risk_factors.title: Integration Security Gaps
risk_factors.description: Integrations with Teams, Zoom, Google Meet are mentioned but no security considerations (OAuth scopes, token handling) are provided.
risk_factors.mitigation: Adopt secure OAuth flows, validate third‑party certificates, and enforce least‑privilege scopes for each integration.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: "Meeting Health Score: 68%" is presented without explaining the calculation, weighting, or threshold criteria.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Specify the algorithm, data sources, weighting factors, and confidence intervals used to compute the score.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.issue: Ambiguous definition of "Bias" in Workplace Fairness Detector.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: Feature states it "Detects bias in promotions, rewards, opportunities, performance reviews" but does not define which protected attributes are considered.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: List the protected classes (e.g., gender, ethnicity) and describe the statistical tests or thresholds used to flag bias.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: The document claims the system is an "autonomous HR analyst" yet also describes a "human‑in‑the‑loop" dashboard for executives.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Clarify the decision‑making boundaries: which actions are fully automated versus which require human approval.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.issue: Vague description of "Policy Gap Detector" output.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: Example shows "48 employees asked about WFH" and a "Policy Clarity Score: Low" without defining the scoring rubric.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Provide a clear scoring model, thresholds for low/medium/high, and remediation workflow.

missing_sections_and_details.section_name: System Architecture Overview & Data Flow Diagram
missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Without an architecture diagram, engineers cannot assess component boundaries, integration points, or data residency, leading to design rework and security blind spots.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Include a high‑level diagram showing data ingestion (meeting transcripts, surveys), AI processing pipelines, storage layers, APIs to Teams/Zoom/Google Meet, and the executive dashboard. Detail technology stack (e.g., cloud provider, container orchestration, database).

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The platform handles personal and health‑related employee data; lack of privacy controls exposes the organization to regulatory fines and reputational damage.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Add a dedicated NFR section covering data encryption, consent management, right‑to‑be‑forgotten, data residency, breach notification, and regular privacy impact assessments.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: AI decisions affect career progression and compensation; without explainability, decisions may be contested and could lead to discrimination lawsuits.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define model interpretability techniques (SHAP, LIME), bias audit schedule, and a process for providing human‑readable explanations to affected employees.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Real‑time analysis of meeting transcripts and large‑scale sentiment processing require clear performance targets; missing NFRs risk system overload.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specify latency (<2 seconds per transcript), throughput (e.g., 10 k meetings/day), 99.9% uptime, and autoscaling rules.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No test cases, validation criteria, or acceptance metrics are provided, making verification impossible.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Create unit, integration, and end‑to‑end test suites; define acceptance thresholds for model accuracy (e.g., F1 > 0.85 for sentiment), false‑positive rates for bias detection, and UI usability tests.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The document lists features but does not map them to business goals, technical components, or test cases, hindering compliance and auditability.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Provide a table linking each requirement ID to business objective, responsible subsystem, verification method, and status.

rtm_matrix.business_goal: Provide real‑time meeting sentiment analysis to improve team health.
rtm_matrix.test_case_verification: Validate that transcript ingestion + sentiment model returns a health score within ±5% of manually annotated baseline on 100 test meetings.

rtm_matrix.business_goal: Detect manager effectiveness for targeted coaching.
rtm_matrix.test_case_verification: Cross‑validate AI score against 12‑month HR performance review outcomes; require correlation coefficient ≥0.7.
Precision @10% ≥ 0.80 when compared to HR promotion decisions over the past year.

rtm_matrix.business_goal: Detect bias in compensation and promotion processes.
rtm_matrix.test_case_verification: Run statistical parity tests on simulated data; flagging must occur when disparity >5% for protected groups.

rtm_matrix.business_goal: Provide executives with an AI‑driven strategic dashboard.
rtm_matrix.test_case_verification: User acceptance test with 5 senior HR leaders confirming that all key metrics (trust score, burnout risk, attrition forecast) are displayed and drill‑down works.

ai_recommendations: Add a comprehensive Architecture & Data Flow section with security boundaries, cloud services, and integration protocols.
Develop a full Security and Privacy NFR chapter covering GDPR/HIPAA compliance, encryption, consent, data retention, and incident response.
Create a Traceability Matrix linking every AI feature to business objectives, technical components, test cases, and compliance checks; update status as development progresses.
